findings.title: Google Meet bookings without a destination calendar now throw before falling back
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` can produce an empty array, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`. A booking with Google Meet selected but no destination calendar now evaluates `.integration` on `undefined` and throws instead of following the previous Cal Video fallback path. This also fails strict null checking. Use optional access or explicitly handle an empty array.

findings.title: Collective host calendars are discarded when the primary host has no calendar
findings.body: The event initializes `destinationCalendar` as `null` when neither the event type nor the first organizer has a destination calendar, then adds collective hosts with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`. In that case the optional call does nothing, even if later collective hosts have configured calendars. Such a collective booking creates no calendar events for those hosts; initialize an empty array before appending host destinations.

findings.title: Later destination calendars are created using the first host's target in several providers
findings.body: The loop invokes `createEvent` with the complete destination-calendar array for every host rather than an event narrowed to the current `destination`. Office 365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService all select `event.destinationCalendar[0]`, so when processing a second host they authenticate as that host but attempt to create in the first host's calendar (usually failing with access errors or creating in a shared wrong calendar). Passing the target external ID only to `CalendarManager` does not fix this because it is not forwarded to those provider create calls. Each provider invocation must be given or select the current destination.

findings.title: Legacy destinations without a credential ID lose their external calendar ID in references
findings.body: The branch for a destination with no `credentialId` calls `createEvent(c, event)` without `destination.externalId`. `CalendarManager` therefore returns an `EventResult` with no `externalId`, and the new reference-building code persists that missing value rather than the selected destination ID. Subsequent update/delete operations cannot address the original calendar and may default to the primary calendar. This branch exists specifically to support destinations without credential IDs, so it must pass and preserve the current destination external ID.

findings.title: New video references no longer retain their credential ID
findings.body: For a non-calendar result, including every dedicated video meeting result, this now writes `credentialId: undefined`. Previously it retained `result.credentialId`. Cancellation only deletes a video meeting when its booking reference has a credential ID, so newly created Zoom/Teams/etc. meetings will be left behind on cancellation; other later operations also cannot reliably select the credential. Keep `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results.

findings.title: Persisting only the first destination prevents delayed collective scheduling for other hosts
findings.body: A booking stores only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` in the scalar `Booking.destinationCalendar` relation. Required-confirmation and payment flows later reconstruct their CalendarEvent by wrapping that scalar in a one-element array (for example, `confirm.handler.ts`), with no remaining source for the other collective hosts' destinations. As a result, collective bookings scheduled after approval or payment only create the first host's calendar event. Persist all destinations or reconstruct them from the event type's hosts in every delayed scheduling path.

findings.title: Cancelling all occurrences of a collective recurring booking leaves other host events behind
findings.body: For each calendar reference, the recurring-cancellation branch iterates only the booking owner's calendar credentials and then calls `find` to select the first calendar reference of each updated booking. With multiple host references, every outer iteration repeatedly deletes that first reference using the owner's credentials; references belonging to the other hosts are never selected with their own credentials. Their recurring calendar events remain after the booking is marked cancelled. Iterate each updated booking reference and resolve its `credentialId` before deleting it.

findings.title: Rescheduling deletes multi-host calendar events with an arbitrary credential
findings.body: Credentials are stored in `credentialsMap` keyed only by integration type. A collective booking can now have multiple references of the same type, such as two `google_calendar` references owned by different hosts, but the map retains only one credential. The deletion loop then uses that one credential for every reference of the type, causing authorization failures and leaving other hosts' old events intact. Resolve credentials by each reference's `credentialId` instead of calendar type.

findings.title: Organization slug persistence was reversed for team-billing deployments
findings.body: This changes the previous condition from storing `slug` when team billing is disabled to storing it only when team billing is enabled. Consequently, non-billing deployments create organizations without their requested team slug even though slug collision and domain setup were performed, breaking slug-based organization routing. It also stores both `slug` and `requestedSlug` when billing is enabled, contrary to the prior deferred-slug behavior.

findings.title: The public webhook payload changes destinationCalendar from object/null to array without compatibility handling
findings.body: CalendarEvent is serialized in developer webhook payloads, as shown by the changed webhook E2E expectation. Existing webhook consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.integration` or expect `null` will now receive an array/empty array in flows rebuilt from a booking, while newly created bookings can still emit `null`. This is an externally observable schema break and also creates inconsistent shapes across lifecycle events; preserve the webhook contract or version/document the payload migration.
